seo.title: 30 Essential Tools for ZK Engineers
seo.description: A curated list of tools for zero-knowledge engineers covering proof systems, circuit development, and ZK application frameworks.

content.intro: Zero-knowledge engineering requires specialized tools for developing circuits, generating proofs, and building ZK applications. Here are the essentials.

items.name: Circom
items.description: Domain-specific language for writing arithmetic circuits. Free and open-source.

items.name: Noir
items.description: Rust-like language for ZK applications from Aztec. Free and open-source.

items.name: Halo2
items.description: Rust framework for writing PLONK-based circuits. Free and open-source.

items.name: Leo
items.description: Programming language for Aleo's private applications. Free and open-source.

items.name: Cairo
items.description: Language for writing provable programs for StarkNet. Free and open-source.

items.name: o1js
items.description: TypeScript library for writing Mina zkApps. Free and open-source.

items.name: SnarkJS
items.description: JavaScript implementation of zkSNARKs. Works with Circom. Free and open-source. Active open-source project on GitHub.

items.name: arkworks
items.description: Rust libraries for SNARKs including Groth16 and Marlin. Free and open-source.

items.name: Plonky2
items.description: Recursive SNARK system from Polygon. Very fast. Check the GitHub repo for documentation and examples.

items.name: Plonky3
items.description: modern proving system. Modular and flexible. Check the GitHub repo for documentation and examples.

items.name: Risc0
items.description: ZK-VM based on RISC-V. Prove arbitrary computation. Free and open-source.

items.name: SP1
items.description: High-performance zkVM from Succinct Labs. Check the GitHub repo for documentation and examples.

sections.heading: Development and Testing
sections.description: Tools for developing and testing circuits.

items.name: circomlib
items.description: Library of common Circom components. Check the GitHub repo for documentation and examples.

items.name: Hardhat Circom
items.description: Hardhat plugin for Circom development. Check the GitHub repo for documentation and examples.

items.name: Nargo
items.description: Package manager and CLI for Noir. Worth evaluating for your workflow.

items.name: Scarb
items.description: Build toolchain and package manager for Cairo. Free and open-source.

items.name: Protostar
items.description: Development framework for StarkNet contracts. Free and open-source.

items.name: bn254
items.description: BN254 curve implementation. Most common for SNARKs. Free and open-source. Active open-source project on GitHub.

items.name: Poseidon Hash
items.description: ZK-friendly hash function implementations. Check the GitHub repo for documentation and examples.

items.name: blstrs
items.description: BLS12-381 implementation for BLS signatures and SNARKs. Free and open-source. Active open-source project on GitHub.

items.name: ff
items.description: Finite field arithmetic traits and implementations. Free and open-source. Active open-source project on GitHub.

items.name: Semaphore
items.description: Anonymous signaling protocol. Foundation for many ZK apps. Free and open-source.

items.name: ZK Email
items.description: Prove email ownership without revealing content. Free and open-source.

items.name: Worldcoin SDK
items.description: Integration with World ID for proof of personhood. Free and open-source.

items.name: Axiom
items.description: ZK coprocessor for accessing historical blockchain data. Used by production teams across the ecosystem.

items.name: Brevis
items.description: ZK coprocessor for cross-chain data and computation. Used by production teams across the ecosystem.

items.name: ZK Hack
items.description: Community and learning platform for ZK developers. Free and open-source.

items.name: ZK Whiteboard Sessions
items.description: Video series explaining ZK concepts. Worth evaluating for your workflow.

items.name: Ingopedia
items.description: Curated ZK learning resources. Worth evaluating for your workflow.

items.name: Awesome ZKP
items.description: Curated list of ZK resources and projects. Check the GitHub repo for documentation and examples.

proTips.tip: Start with Circom to understand circuit constraints before moving to lower-level libraries.
zkVMs like SP1 and Risc0 let you write normal Rust instead of circuits.
Understand the tradeoffs between different proof systems (proving time vs verification cost vs proof size).
Poseidon is faster than Keccak in circuits. Use ZK-friendly primitives.
Test constraint counts carefully. Small changes can dramatically affect proof times.
